note: Both lost games (seeds 101 and 202) ended the same way. After a pop, the new dot sat at 179 degrees and the bar came at it counterclockwise from the -180 side. The extractor called the landings -177/-180 'edge', because it counted a bar exactly on the 180-degree line as a possible pop. It also called waiting 'gameOver', because the dot's pixel-rounded angle (179.04) put the later 174-degree landing 0.04 degrees outside the 5-degree window. The end screens show the bar stopped on the line (seed 101) and at -177 (seed 202), both misses, while a tap one frame later (landing at 177 or 174) was a sure pop. Now a landing on the line counts as a miss (the game reads it as -180), and dot angles are snapped back to the whole degrees the game uses. tapOutcome and waitOutcome now come from a short look-ahead that weighs both possible landings and the chance that the next decision comes two frames later (shown as tapChance and waitChance), so a doubtful tap is taken only when no later moment is better. The rule becomes: tap when tapOutcome is pop or edge and waitOutcome is farther or gameOver. New tests pin the seam approach on both failure windows, keep the good pops before them, and add an invariant that a tap landing on or across the line never counts as a pop or edge.
instructions:
Pop the Lock. A bar spins around the centre of a ring and a dot sits on the ring. Tap while the bar is on the dot to pop it: the bar then turns the other way and the dot jumps elsewhere on the ring. Tapping while the bar is off the dot, or letting the bar pass the dot, ends the game. Pop as many dots as you can.
TIMING. The game never pauses. The bar turns stepDeg degrees (3) per animation frame (about 16.7 ms) in direction dir. A tap lands about 45 ms after the frame it is decided on, after two or three more frames (three more often), so by then the bar has turned about leadDeg further (about 8 degrees; 0 when the game waits for every decision). Every bar position below is where the bar will be WHEN A TAP DECIDED NOW LANDS, not where it is drawn. Decisions come about one frame apart, but about one in five comes two frames later, so the moment one frame ahead can be skipped.
FIELDS. barAngleDeg: expected bar angle when a tap decided now lands. dotAngleDeg: the dot angle as measured (the game puts dots on whole degrees; the gaps use that whole-degree angle). gapDeg: degrees that landing is still short of the dot centre (negative = past it). gapNextDeg: the same for a tap decided one frame later. ticksToDot: frames until the landing reaches the dot centre. barMoving: the bar moved since the last decision. barReversed: the bar just changed direction, which means a dot was just popped. dotMoving: the dot just jumped to a new place. dotPopped: the dot shown is the one just popped; the new dot has not appeared yet. popPending: a tap decided at the last tap moment may still be on its way (a second tap would end the game). popTolDeg (5): a landing within this of the dot centre, on the dot's side of the 180-degree line and not on it, is a sure pop. edgeTolDeg (about 8): a landing between popTolDeg and this only touches the dot's edge and may or may not pop.
THE 180-DEGREE LINE (the leftmost point of the ring): the game compares raw angles from -180 to 180 and reads a bar exactly on the line as -180, so a landing across the line from the dot, or exactly on the line, is a miss. seamSplit: a possible landing is across the line from the dot. barOnSeam: a possible landing is exactly on the line. dotOnSeam: the dot sits exactly on the line, so every landing near it is a coin flip.
tapChance (0-100): how likely a tap decided now is to pop the dot, weighing its two possible landings (a sure pop counts 90-100, more the nearer the centre; an edge landing 10-50; a miss 0). waitChance: the same for waiting and tapping at the best later moment, allowing for the next decision coming one, two or three frames later.
tapOutcome = what a tap decided now does: 'pop' = sure pop (every possible landing is a sure-pop position); 'edge' = it may pop (some landing can pop, but not every landing is a sure pop); 'miss' = it ends the game (no landing can pop); 'uncertain' = do not tap: the bar did not move or just reversed, the dot just jumped or was just popped, or popPending is true; 'none' = the game is over.
waitOutcome = what waiting does, compared with tapping now: 'safe' = the bar is still approaching (a tap one frame later still lands short of the sure-pop window) and waiting is at least as good (also when there is no live dot); 'closer' = waiting is better than tapping now (waitChance above tapChance); 'farther' = tapping now is about as good as waiting or better, and a tap one frame later would still be a sure pop; 'gameOver' = tapping now is about as good as waiting or better, and a tap one frame later would no longer be a sure pop (last good chance).
RULES, in order: 1) gameOver is true -> wait. 2) tapOutcome is 'pop' or 'edge' and waitOutcome is 'farther' or 'gameOver' -> tap. 3) Otherwise -> wait. Never tap when tapOutcome is 'miss', 'uncertain' or 'none', or when waitOutcome is 'safe' or 'closer'. pops counts the dots popped so far; unknown lists unrecognised objects, which are not threats.

actions.description: Click the game once. If the bar is on the dot when the click lands, this pops it (the bar reverses and the dot jumps). If not, the game ends.
Do nothing for this decision and let the bar keep turning.

tests.expect: !(state.barAngleDeg === -168 && state.dotAngleDeg === -176.1) || state.gameOver || (state.dotPopped === true && state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge')
tests.why: One frame after a pop, the bar had reversed but the popped dot was still drawn at -176.1. v1 said 'pop', tapped again and lost. That dot must now be marked as popped and not tappable.

tests.expect: !(state.barAngleDeg === -15 && state.dotAngleDeg === -8.9) || state.gameOver || (state.dotPopped === true && state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge')
tests.why: Same double-tap failure: the bar reversed from -12 to -15 while the popped dot stayed at -8.9.

tests.expect: !(state.barAngleDeg === 177 && state.dotAngleDeg === -177.1) || state.gameOver || (state.seamSplit === true && state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge' && state.waitOutcome === 'closer')
tests.why: A tap with the bar at 177 and the dot at -177.1, on opposite sides of the +/-180 line, ended the game. The bar must wait until it crosses to the dot's side, which is also nearer the dot centre.

tests.expect: !(state.barAngleDeg === -114 && state.dotAngleDeg === -112.9) || (state.tapOutcome === 'pop' && (state.waitOutcome === 'farther' || state.waitOutcome === 'gameOver'))
tests.why: Keeps a known good pop: the bar 1.1 degrees from a settled dot and about to pass it must still be 'pop' at its best moment.

tests.expect: !(state.barAngleDeg === -12 && state.dotAngleDeg === -8.9) || state.tapOutcome === 'pop'
tests.why: Keeps a known good pop: the bar 3.1 degrees before a settled dot, on the same side of the 180 line, must be recognised as poppable.

tests.expect: !(Math.abs(state.barAngleDeg) === 180 && state.dotAngleDeg === -179) || state.gameOver || (state.barOnSeam === true && state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.waitOutcome !== 'gameOver')
tests.why: v2 tapped here and lost. The bar sat exactly on the 180-degree line (the old extractor showed -180) with the dot at -179, and the game counted the bar on the +180 side. A bar on the line must never be a sure pop. The next frame (-177) is a sure pop on the dot's side, so waiting must not be flagged as the last chance.

tests.expect: !(state.barAngleDeg === 177 && state.dotAngleDeg === -179) || state.gameOver || (state.seamSplit === true && state.tapOutcome === 'miss' && state.waitOutcome === 'closer')
tests.why: One frame earlier the bar is at 177, across the 180-degree line from the dot at -179. A tap there misses, and waiting leads through the line to a sure pop at -177.

tests.expect: state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' || (state.barOnSeam === false && state.seamSplit === false && state.dotOnSeam === false && Math.abs(state.gapDeg) <= state.popTolDeg)
tests.why: Invariant: a sure pop never has the bar or the dot on the 180-degree line or across it, and is always inside the sure-pop window.

tests.expect: state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' || (state.barOnSeam === false && state.seamSplit === false && state.dotOnSeam === false && Math.abs(state.gapDeg) <= state.popTolDeg)
tests.why: Same invariant on the first seam failure (bar 177, dot -177.1), which was recorded at the older, coarser tick.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === -26.1 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg - 9.9) < 0.3) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.leadDeg > 8.8 || state.gameOver || (state.tapOutcome === 'pop' && (state.waitOutcome === 'farther' || state.waitOutcome === 'gameOver'))
tests.why: v3 ignored the ~45 ms input lag. It waited on this frame (bar drawn 9.9 deg before the dot) and tapped two decisions later at 2.1 deg past, and the tap landed about 11 deg past the dot. A tap lands two or three frames later (leadDeg about 8), so this frame lands 1-4 deg before the centre and must be the tap moment.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === -26.1 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg - 3.9) < 0.3) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.leadDeg > 8.8 || state.gameOver || (state.popPending === true && state.tapOutcome === 'uncertain')
tests.why: The decision after the tap moment (bar drawn 3.9 deg before the dot, 22 ms later) comes before a tap made at the tap moment can land. It must be popPending/uncertain so no second tap follows the pop.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === -26.1 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg + 2.1) < 0.3) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.tapOutcome !== 'pop'
tests.why: v3 tapped here (bar drawn 2.1 deg past the dot) as a 'pop' and lost. With the lag the tap lands 8-11 deg past the dot, so it can never be a sure pop.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === -31 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg + 2) < 0.3) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.tapOutcome !== 'pop'
tests.why: v3 tapped with the bar drawn 2 deg past the dot at -31 and lost (the end screen shows the bar about 11 deg past). The landing is 8-11 deg past, so this frame must not be a sure pop.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === -31 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg - 7) < 0.3) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.leadDeg > 8.8 || state.gameOver || state.popPending === true || (state.tapOutcome === 'pop' && (state.waitOutcome === 'farther' || state.waitOutcome === 'gameOver'))
tests.why: v3 waited here as 'edge'/'closer' (bar drawn 7 deg before the dot). With the lag a tap lands 1 deg before to 2 deg past the centre, so this frame (or the one just before it, leaving this one popPending) is the tap moment.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === 177.1 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg - 5.9) < 0.3) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.leadDeg > 8.8 || state.gameOver || state.popPending === true || (state.tapOutcome === 'pop' && state.waitOutcome === 'gameOver')
tests.why: The bar is drawn at -177, on the far side of the 180-degree line from the dot at 177.1. v3 called it a miss. A tap here lands after the bar crosses the line, at 177 or 174 (0.1-3.1 deg past the centre, on the dot's side), so it is a sure pop and the last one.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === 177.1 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg + 6.1) < 0.3) || state.leadDeg < 6 || (state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge')
tests.why: v3 tapped here as 'edge' (bar drawn 6.1 deg past the dot) and lost. With the lag the tap lands 12-15 deg past, so it is a certain miss.

tests.expect: state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' || (state.barOnSeam === false && state.seamSplit === false && state.dotOnSeam === false && Math.abs(state.gapDeg) <= state.popTolDeg)
tests.why: Invariant with the lag: a sure pop never lands on or across the 180-degree line and always lands inside the sure-pop window. This window crosses the line.

tests.expect: state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' || (state.barOnSeam === false && state.seamSplit === false && state.dotOnSeam === false && Math.abs(state.gapDeg) <= state.popTolDeg)
tests.why: The same landing invariant on a real-time window with three pops and reversals.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === 179 && state.dir === 'counterclockwise' && state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg > 8.5 && state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg < 17) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.leadDeg > 8.8 || state.gameOver || state.popPending === true || (state.seamSplit === true && state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge' && state.waitOutcome === 'closer')
tests.why: v4 tapped here as edge/gameOver and lost. The new dot sat at 179 and the bar, drawn at -171, would land at -177 (across the 180-degree line) or exactly on the line, which the game reads as -180; the end screen shows the bar stopped on the line. Every landing on this approach misses, and a sure pop (landings 177 and 174) is still ahead, so these frames must be a miss with waitOutcome closer.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === 179 && state.dir === 'counterclockwise' && state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg > 8.5 && state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg < 17) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.leadDeg > 8.8 || state.gameOver || state.popPending === true || (state.seamSplit === true && state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge' && state.waitOutcome === 'closer')
tests.why: Same seam failure on seed 202: the end screen shows the bar stopped at -177, across the line from the dot at 179. The approach frames must be a miss with waitOutcome closer, because the landings 177/174 on the dot's side come later.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === -102.8 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg - 5) < 0.4) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.leadDeg > 8.8 || state.gameOver || state.popPending === true || (state.tapOutcome === 'pop' && (state.waitOutcome === 'farther' || state.waitOutcome === 'gameOver'))
tests.why: Keeps the good pop just before the seam failure: the bar drawn 5 degrees before the dot at -103 lands 1-4 degrees past its centre, a sure pop and the last one, so it must stay the tap moment after the dot-angle snapping and look-ahead changes.

tests.expect: !(state.dotAngleDeg === -125 && Math.abs(state.gapDeg + state.leadDeg - 7) < 0.4) || state.leadDeg < 6 || state.leadDeg > 8.8 || state.gameOver || state.popPending === true || (state.tapOutcome === 'pop' && (state.waitOutcome === 'farther' || state.waitOutcome === 'gameOver'))
tests.why: Keeps the good pop before the seed-202 seam failure: the bar drawn 7 degrees before the dot at -125 lands 1 degree before to 2 degrees past its centre. That frame must be a tap moment, or be popPending if the frame before was already one.

tests.expect: state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' || (state.barOnSeam === false && state.seamSplit === false && state.dotOnSeam === false && Math.abs(state.gapDeg) <= state.popTolDeg)
tests.why: Landing invariant on the new seam failure window: a sure pop never lands on or across the 180-degree line and always lands inside the sure-pop window.

tests.expect: state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' || (state.barOnSeam === false && state.seamSplit === false && state.dotOnSeam === false && Math.abs(state.gapDeg) <= state.popTolDeg)
tests.why: The same landing invariant on the second seam failure window.

tests.expect: !(state.seamSplit === true && state.barOnSeam === true) || state.dotOnSeam === true || (state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge')
tests.why: When one possible landing is across the 180-degree line from the dot and the other is exactly on it (read by the game as -180), every landing misses. v4 called this 'edge' and tapped; it must never be pop or edge.

tests.expect: !(state.seamSplit === true && state.barOnSeam === true) || state.dotOnSeam === true || (state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge')
tests.why: Same rule on seed 202, where the tap landed at -177 across the line: a tap whose landings are all across the line or on it can never pop.

tests.expect: !(state.seamSplit === true && state.barOnSeam === true) || state.dotOnSeam === true || (state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge')
tests.why: The same seam rule on the earlier window where the bar crossed the 180-degree line towards a dot at 177: landings across the line or on it are misses.
